whatis.intro: Landed cost is what a product costs you at your dock: the supplier's price plus the freight and fees to get it there. Split per unit, it lets you compare supplier offers that come in different case sizes. It is the number to rank on, not the quoted price.

cards.title: Case price plus freight, per unit
cards.body: The case price plus freight per case, split across the units inside. Option C's $19.00 case lands at $20.20, which is $2.02 a unit.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the case price and freight that landed cost counts

cards.title: The cash a bigger case ties up
cards.body: The cost of holding what you bought. A 24 unit case can win on landed cost and still tie up more cash and warehouse space while it sells through.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for the holding cost a bigger case adds

cards.title: A backhaul still has a freight cost
cards.body: If your own truck collects the order on a return trip, freight is not zero. Put your truck's cost for that stop in the freight box, split down to the case.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for the freight cost of a pickup on your own truck

look.h2: Match the quotes before ranking landed cost
look.intro: The division is exact. The quotes you feed it are not always alike, and these three gaps are the usual reason.

steps.title: The same item in all three quotes
steps.body: Check grade, brand and spec before you rank. A cheaper unit of a lower grade is a different product, and the ranking cannot tell the difference.

steps.title: Prices that hold for the same term
steps.body: A spot price good for this week and a contract price held for a year do not belong in one ranking. Note how long each quote stands.

steps.title: A price you can actually buy at
steps.body: Each quote assumes you meet its terms. If the cheapest unit depends on a volume tier above your 6,000 units a month, that price is not on offer.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits next to a supplier decision
vos.h3: Your units a month start with what accounts order
vos.body: VOS does not compare supplier quotes or buy stock. The units a month you enter come from what your accounts order, and that is the side it works on. Each order placed in the VOS app arrives with a number, a date and a timestamp.
